# v0.10.1 beta - C++ renderer

This beta includes the C++ renderer introduced in v0.10.0, plus improved audio/timing at lower display refresh rates and animated target acquisition. Since these releases are back to back, the main v0.10.0 changes are included below.

## New in v0.10.1

- Fix sustained audio starvation with blocking V-sync in tested 60 Hz configurations. DOSBox-X now retains short timer catch-up debt and defers presentation while catching up.
- Improve graphics-time accounting so automatic CPU cycles no longer collapse during the reproduced slow mission-loading case, including its fallback to the DOS loading screen.
- Add animated targeting brackets with configurable acquisition duration, rotation, and translucent trails. Zero duration disables the animation; zero trail length disables trails.
- Remove the separate 60 FPS max-cycles launcher. The ordinary launchers remain available.
- Clarify first-time installation and upgrades. Development diagnostics are opt-in; their comparison helper is not included in the player package.

The bundled DOSBox-X host is v0.3.1. These fixes retain synchronous V-sync; automatic monitor-rate selection is not included. Choose a target at or below 75 FPS compatible with your display, such as 60 FPS at 60 Hz or 72 FPS at 144 Hz.

## Main changes introduced in v0.10.0

- C++ enhanced renderer with full scene rendering, HUD, weapon effects, view modes, and HUD damage effects. The previous release measured approximately 3-4x the performance of the Python renderer on a high-end CPU/GPU; performance depends on hardware and scene.
- Direct game-resource loading with a visible diagnostic and guest-memory fallback if the archive cannot be loaded.
- Mission frame pacing in original DOS and side-by-side views as well as enhanced view.
- Improved resource and OpenGL-context cleanup, plus visible configuration-startup errors.
- Smaller Python runtime: Python remains for joystick input, gameplay fixes, and configuration; NumPy, Numba, and the Python OpenGL renderer are no longer required.
- Renderer and FreeType source and dependency notices accompany the release. Matching DOSBox-X source is available from [the v0.3.1 source snapshot](https://github.com/furious-pixel/dosbox-x-mod/archive/refs/tags/v0.3.1.zip).

**Supported platform:** Windows x64 on Intel or AMD 64-bit hardware.

## Installation and upgrade

**First-time installation**

Extract the release into a fresh directory, run `./configure.bat`, and follow
the onscreen instructions to install and configure the game.

**Updating from an earlier installation**

Extract the release into a fresh directory, then copy these from your previous
installation:

- The `game/` directory.
- `mw2mods/mod.conf`.
- `mw2mods/joystick.conf`, if present.

You can then launch the game without running the configurator again.
